Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 95, verses 1–8:

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–3} {At-Tin} is the well-known fig, and likewise {az-Zaytun} (the olive). He swears by these two trees because of the abundance of the benefits of their wood and fruit, and because their domain in the land of al-Sham is the place of the prophethood of 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him). {Wa Tur Sinin}: that is, Mount Sinai (Tur Sina'), the place of the prophethood of Musa (peace be upon him). {Wa hadha al-baladi al-amin}: this is Makkah al-Mukarramah, the place of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). Thus Allah, the Exalted, swears by these sacred places which He chose and from which He sent forth the best and most noble of the prophets.

{4} The sworn-to matter is His saying: {Laqad khalaqna al-insana fi ahsani taqwim} ("We have certainly created man in the best of stature"); that is, in complete creation, proportionate in its limbs, upright in its form, lacking nothing it needs, outwardly and inwardly.

{5–6} Despite these great blessings, which require that he give thanks for them, most of creation turns away from thanking the Benefactor, occupied with amusement and play, having contented themselves with the lowest of matters and the basest of character. So Allah returns them {to the lowest of the low} (asfal safilin); that is, to the lowest part of the Fire, the place of the sinners who rebel against their Lord. Except for those upon whom Allah has bestowed faith, righteous deeds, and lofty, noble character: {for them} is, by that, high ranks, and {a reward that is never cut off} (ajrun ghayru mamnun); that is, not interrupted, but rather abundant pleasures, continuous joys, and multiplied blessings, in an eternity that does not end and a bliss that does not change, whose fruit is constant and whose shade is everlasting.

{7–8} {So what causes you yet to deny the Recompense?} (fama yukadhdhibuka ba'du bi'd-din); that is: what is it that makes you, O man, deny the Day of Recompense for deeds? You have already seen many of the signs of Allah which should produce certainty in you, and of His blessings which oblige you not to disbelieve in any of them. {Is not Allah the most just of judges?} (alaysa Allahu bi-ahkam al-hakimin): Does His wisdom require that He leave creation neglected, not commanded, not forbidden, not rewarded, not punished? Or is it that He who created man in stages, stage after stage, and bestowed upon them blessings, good, and kindness that they cannot count, and raised them with fine upbringing, must surely return them to an abode which is their resting place and their ultimate goal, toward which they aim and to which they turn?

Finished. And praise be to Allah.
